Subject: Reserved capacity proposal — SageHealth (index-trigger proposal)

Hi Aisha / Peter,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — appreciated the detail on SageHealth's inference mix and the phased rollout plan. Attached is our formal reserved capacity proposal (v1). Key points called out up front:

- Proposal: 200 reserved A100-equivalent GPU-hours/day (phased activation over 6 months) with a 24-month tenor.
- Pricing: baseline unit rate with a consumer-price-index style trigger for GPU-cost pass-through. We proposed a +/- 12% corridor on base unit price tied to our published GPU price index (monthly).
- Protection: 3-month grace window before any upward index adjustment applies for new production activations.
- Fallback: automated model-variant routing (lower-precision quantized variants) to cap peak spend during transient market spikes.

Attachments: SageHealth_Reserved_Proposal_v1.pdf (application/pdf), SageHealth_CAPEX-OpEx_breakdown.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Ask: please confirm whether procurement prefers an absolute cap on upward adjustments (we proposed 18% absolute cap) or a scheduled review cadence. Also flag any legal/finance constraints we should route for approval.

Next step: if the approach looks ok, I'll ask finance to pre-authorize an escalation ladder for discounts/credits if GPU input costs move beyond the corridor.

Best,
Priyom

Priyom —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear summary. A few quick notes from our side:

1) Procurement will want an absolute ceiling on any upward pass-through. The team is sympathetic to market volatility but a hard cap (we suggested 15%) is a non-starter unless paired with a meaningful crediting mechanism when prices fall.
2) Finance wants to see the cap tied to a clear benchmark (your published index is fine) and an escalation path for any upward moves to be approved by our CFO if >10%.
3) For rollout safety, we like the phased activation but want a clause that allows a temporary pause on activation if spot-market costs spike >20% month-over-month.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can commit to (a) a 15% hard cap on upward adjustments, and (b) a credit mechanism that refunds the difference if your index falls below the base for two consecutive months?

Also copied procurement — Peter, can you share your standard redlines for index-linked pricing?

Regards,
Aisha Gupta
Head of Platform, SageHealth

Folks — quick take from commercial ops and product ops:

- Commercial fallback ladder (no exec escalation up to +20% index move):
  * 0–10% increase: automatic surcharge per index; no customer credits; Redwood covers transient variance via buffer pool.
  * 10–15% increase: apply surcharge; offer a 4% pre-negotiated credit (applied retroactively for the month) if customer keeps phased activations live.
  * 15–20% increase: require finance sign-off for further surcharge; offer model-variant routing to reduce consumption by 30% and a sliding credit between 6–10% depending on retained capacity.
- Above +20%: trigger exec review and SalesOps escalation.

On the downside (index declines): propose a crediting mechanism where any cumulative negative deviation of >5% over two months triggers a refund equal to 50% of the per-unit differential for that period (applied as account credit). That aligns with their request while capping our downside.

Operational note: product can implement automated model-variant routing and a pause-signal for phased activation; however, pauses must be communicated 72 hours in advance (to avoid wasted pre-provisioning).

I'll draft the clause language and a simple table for procurement to review. If Finance (Neha) can pre-authorize the 6–10% sliding credit band for 15–20% index moves, we avoid exec escalation.

-ben

Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — finance position below:

- We can pre-authorize the 4% credit for the 10–15% band without exec approval.
- For the 15–20% band, Finance can pre-authorize up to an 8% sliding credit, but we need a cap on cumulative credits across the 24-month term (proposal: 6% of total committed value as a credit reserve). Anything above that requires VP Sales + CFO sign-off.
- On the downside crediting mechanism: approve the 50% refund of differential, but limit to a 4% annualized net exposure to Redwood (we should model the P&L impact — I'll attach a quick sensitivity table).

I'll prepare a short Finance sign-off memo and a deal-level P&L sensitivity for review. From an accounting perspective, the 3-month activation grace window is reasonable; however, do not promise more than 90 days for pausing activations without re-baselining resource allocation.

Aisha / Peter —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Short summary of what Redwood can commit to without exec escalation:

1) Upward moves: a hard ceiling at +20% will trigger exec review. For day-to-day handling we can accept a 15% customer-requested hard cap if SageHealth accepts the following:
   - Redwood will provide a pre-negotiated credit reserve equal to 6% of the total committed value to offset downside volatility and to fund retrospective credits (per Finance).
   - Operational fallbacks: automated model-variant routing that can reduce consumption by ~30% during spikes; phased activation pause with 72 hours notice.
2) For increases in the 10–15% range we will apply surcharge and a 4% retroactive credit if activations remain live. For the 15–20% range we can apply a sliding credit up to 8% (Finance pre-authorized up to 8% but the cumulative credit reserve is capped at 6% of total committed value).
3) Downside credits: if the index falls below base for two consecutive months, we will issue a credit equal to 50% of the per-unit differential for that period, subject to the cumulative cap noted above.

Next steps:
- If this approach is acceptable, I'll circulate proposed clause language for inclusion in the SOW and send a DocuSign envelope for signature (term: 24 months, phased activation schedule).
- Ben / Marissa will attach the fallback SLA table for procurement to review.
- Neha will attach the finance sensitivity memo for SageHealth's CFO.

If SageHealth confirms acceptance of the cumulative credit cap and pause notification cadence, we can proceed to DocuSign and aim to get this executed next week.

Best regards,
